title: The Schmosby Pool
logline: Punchy renews his vows in New York and asks Ted to be his best man again, and Ted swears that this time he'll be a dignified adult named Theodore. The gang bets on the exact moment Schmosby breaks him, while Punchy's tiny, terrifying wife Kelly hands each of them a wedding job they fail in their own special way.
coldOpen: Kids, everybody has a version of themselves that only one old friend can bring out. Mine is named Schmosby. And in the fall of 2013, your aunts and uncles bet eighty dollars on the exact minute he'd show up.

couch.line: Is Schmosby the reason we're not allowed to go to Ohio?

guests.name: Kelly Punciarello
guests.role: Punchy's wife of ten years, a middle-school vice principal from Parma, Ohio. Tiny, soft-spoken and utterly terrifying: never raises her voice, gives orders in one word ('Card.'), hands out detentions to adults, and has everyone saying 'Yes, ma'am' within a minute

guests.name: Nana Dot
guests.role: Kelly's ninety-one-year-old grandmother, who has mailed Ted a Christmas card addressed to 'The Shirtless Boy' every year since the first wedding. Tiny, flirty and unbothered, leads every dance, and is the only person in Ohio charmed by Barney's Ohio slang

scenes.summary: Punchy bursts in, in his wedding suit, to announce he and Kelly are renewing their vows at Rocco's on Mulberry, and asks Ted to be best man again. Ted vows to be a dignified adult: no Schmosby, and please call him Theodore. Flashback to Cleveland, 2003: Ted broke five words into his first toast. The gang opens the Schmosby Pool. Punchy pops back in for his hall pass and Ted barely catches himself.

beats.line: It was a Thursday. Ted was grading papers at the bar, so that everyone could see him grading papers.
Schmosby!
Punchy! Ow. Same arm as 1994. It remembers you.
Punchy. Still in the wedding suit.
Kelly says it's gotta get used to me again. We're renewing our vows Saturday! Ten years!
Punchy, that's wonderful! Where?
Rocco's on Mulberry. Where we had our honeymoon dinner. Kelly cried into the calamari.
And I need my best man again. Schmosby. You in?
Punchy, I'd be honored. But this time, I'm doing it right.
I'm a professor now. You're getting a dignified, adult best man.
Like a butler?
Like a gentleman. And for one weekend, I'd like you to call me Theodore.
Like the chipmunk?
Gotta go. Kelly gave me a hall pass till ten. She's a vice principal. She laminates.
Later, Schmo—
Theodore.
Later, Theodore.
Ted, buddy. We've all seen the video of the first wedding.
That video is out of context.
It's eleven minutes long, Ted. It's mostly context.
I was young. And for the record, I made it through most of the toast. I was poised. Eloquent.
Friends. Family. Matrimony comes from the Latin—
Schmosby!
Punchy! The river's on fire!
The river's on fire!
This shirt is a prison!
Somebody stop that boy.
Not yet, though.
You made it six words.
Seven. And one of them was matrimony.
What's with the river?
The Cuyahoga, in Cleveland. Famously caught fire in 1969. Thirteen times total, actually.
Your home state's battle cry is a chemical spill.
And Kelly's grandmother still sends you a Christmas card every year.
Addressed to The Shirtless Boy.
Wait. Dad took his shirt off at a wedding?
It was 2003, Luke. I had just discovered push-ups.
Okay. Betting pool. Twenty bucks picks the exact moment Schmosby breaks Theodore.
You're betting against my dignity?
Ted, nobody bets on your dignity. The odds are insulting.
I'll take the limo. Before the champagne's open. Schmosby's a lightweight.
The toast. Hand Ted a microphone and Theodore's dead in seven words.
Put me down for never.
I believe in you, buddy.
Aww. That's the sweetest way to lose twenty dollars.
And I'll take eleven fourteen p.m.
Why eleven fourteen?
Two drinks, one slow song and a cousin named Dougie. I've been to an Ohio wedding.
Marshall, your bar doesn't fit on the chart.
beats.title: The Schmosby Pool: minutes until Ted breaks

beats.line: Bet all you want. On Saturday, Schmosby dies.
Schmosby! Forgot my hall pass!
Punch—
Not yet! It's Thursday!
Good evening, Adam.
Night, Theodore.
That was like watching a man return a puppy.

scenes.summary: Saturday, the wedding party rides to Rocco's in Barney's limo. Barney rolls out his studied Ohio slang (pop, sweeper, devil strip). Barney's slot is the limo, so he baits Punchy into the river chant; Lily, protecting her 11:14 slot, saves Ted by asking about cornices. Marshall rode with the cake. Kelly texts everyone their wedding jobs, and Lily realizes she's been assigned to guard the exact minute she bought. Barney's last push, the Cedar Point bumper-car story, nearly cracks Ted, until Ranjit pops the champagne. Punchy gets out sad.

beats.line: Barney's wedding gift to Punchy was his limo. It came with Barney. Marshall rode with the cake.
Punchy, my man. Tonight I work the room in your native tongue. I've been studying Ohio.
No way. Say something Ohio.
Hey there. Can I get you a pop?
Dude. You sound exactly like my uncle Sal.
Pop. Sweeper. Devil strip. Ohio girls won't know what hit them.
Do you even know what a devil strip is?
Don't need to. It sounds like Tuesday at my place.
It's the grass between the sidewalk and the street.
Still works.
Adam, may I say, the ceremony was lovely. The proportions of that arbor were nearly Palladian.
Thanks, Theodore.
He says Theodore like he's reading a ransom note.
So, Punchy. I keep hearing about some river.
Oh! Schmosby, remember? The river's—
Ted! What's the difference between a cornice and a corbel?
Lily, great question. A corbel is a bracket, whereas a cornice crowns the entablature.
Lily! Whose side are you on?
Eleven fourteen's, Barney.
Nobody breaks you before eleven fourteen. Nobody.
That's very comforting, and I'm a little scared of you.
Kelly sent our assignments. There's a reply-by time.
beats.title: Kelly Punciarello

messages.text: Adam's Ohio friends couldn't fly in, so tonight you're my staff.
Marshall: guard the cake. Nobody touches it before ten.
Robin: you're on TV, so you're the MC. Read the cards. Do NOT improvise.
Barney: you're dancing with Nana Dot. All night. She leads.
Lily: after eleven, keep Ted and Adam apart. No exceptions.
Ted: be the best man. Mostly the man part.

beats.line: After eleven, I'm supposed to keep them apart? I bought eleven fourteen!
That's a conflict of interest. You should drop out of the pool.
And you should sleep with one eye open.
Marshall's on cake. He insisted on riding in the van. He said it shouldn't be alone.
Lily, at my birthday, he ate a candle. It was lit.
And do not improvise? I once anchored forty minutes with a moth in my ear.
Who is Nana Dot?
Kelly's grandma. Ninety-one. Broke her hip doing the Electric Slide. Finished the song.
She's the one who sends the cards.
Punchy. Best night you ever had with this guy. Go.
Junior year. Four a.m., we drive to Cedar Point to ride the Magnum. Park's closed.
So we ride bumper cars at the county fair for six hours. Remember, Schmo— Theodore?
I do not. Recall. That.
He's cracking! Look at his face! That's Schmosby trying to get out!
Hello! We have arrived! The champagne is open!
Ranjit! What have you done?
You said open it when we arrive, Mister Barney. We have arrived.
Theodore, one. Schmosby, zero.
Bumper cars were fun, though.
Ted. He looked kind of sad.
He's fine. He's Punchy. Punchy's always fine.
Ranjit, you're fired.
You cannot fire me, Mister Barney. You do not know what you do.

scenes.summary: The reception at Rocco's. Marshall only ate the cake from the back; it's round. Robin MCs like it's the eleven o'clock news and reports the cake crime, Kelly sends Marshall to the kids' table, and Barney's Ohio slang works only on Nana Dot, who leads. Lily stole the run of show and moved the toast to 11:14. At eleven, Lily tries to shove Ted at Punchy and Kelly shuts her down. Kelly corners Ted: she called Shaker Heights High, and nine of Punchy's eleven suspensions read 'somebody was mean to Mosby'. At the toast, Theodore gives up: 'Actually, it's pronounced Schmosby.' Sincere toast, then the river is on fire.

beats.line: The ceremony was short. Punchy's vows were seven words long. Three of them were Kelly.
Lily. This cake looks perfect from the front. Right?
Marshall, why is there a crater in it?
Guarding requires testing, Lily! It's fine! I only ate from the back!
Baby. It's round.
Every side is the back.
Good evening. I'm Robin Scherbatsky. Our top story tonight: Adam and Kelly, still married.
In other news, a cake has been breached. Police are seeking a large man from Minnesota.
Robin. Card.
Yes, ma'am.
Marshall. Detention. Kids' table until the toast.
Kelly, there are no kids here.
Then you'll have plenty of room.
Please welcome the bride's grandmother, Nana Dot, to the dance floor.
Ted. I've worked this room in fluent Ohio for an hour. Every bridesmaid ran.
You told a bridesmaid she had a nice devil strip.
Say sweeper again, sugar.
Sweeper.
Ooh.
Ted, she's leading. Nobody leads Barney Stinson. I've never felt so safe.
Good evening, Nana Dot. Theodore Mosby. Charmed.
You nodded at me. Last time you lifted me over your head.
I've grown, Nana Dot.
We'll see, Shirtless Boy.
Lily, the toast is at ten forty. I'm the MC. I make the schedule.
I took the schedule out of Kelly's purse while she was hugging me. Toast's at eleven fourteen.
You're a monster, and I respect it.
Ted! It's eleven! Punchy's out on the patio, all alone. Go give him a big Ohio hug.
Kelly assigned you to keep us apart after eleven.
Kelly's not the boss of me.
I'm the boss of everyone tonight, Lily.
Yes, ma'am.
Theodore. A word.
Kelly. Lovely ceremony. That arbor was nearly Palladian.
Adam's been learning words for you all week. Cornice. Pilaster. He said entablature to the mailman.
He thinks you're embarrassed of him.
I'm not embarrassed of Punchy. I'm embarrassed of who I am around Punchy.
I'm a vice principal, Ted. I called Shaker Heights High. Vice principals talk.
Adam got eleven suspensions. Nine of them give the same reason.
Somebody was mean to Mosby.
He told me those were for fireworks.
Two were for fireworks.
His name is Adam, Ted. Nobody called him Punchy until somebody was mean to you.
So I don't want Theodore up there. I want whoever that boy got suspended for.
And keep your shirt on.
Yes, ma'am.
And now, the best man. Ladies and gentlemen, Theodore Mosby.
Friends. Family. Matrimony comes from the Latin.
Actually, it's pronounced Schmosby.
In ninth grade, I corrected a substitute's pronunciation of Gaudí. Nobody sat with me for a year.
Then this guy sat with me. Every day. And punched anybody who had a problem with it.
Every decent thing about me, Punchy saw first. Then he defended it. With his fists.
Schmosby. I'm gonna punch you so hard.
Punchy! The river's on fire!
The river's on fire!
Eleven fourteen! Pay up!
It's the toast! You pay up!
Objection!
The kids' table doesn't get objections.

scenes.summary: Two a.m., the after-party on the roof. Lily (11:14), Robin (the toast) and Barney (a crack in the limo) all claim the pool; Marshall lawyers it: Schmosby never broke Ted, Ted chose him, and Marshall's slot was never. Robin reveals Kelly confiscated the pot for the cake. Barney has polka night with Nana Dot. Punchy confesses a tenth suspension, Robin and Lily point out Ted didn't correct anyone all night, and Ted admits he likes Schmosby better. Same arm. Future Ted: he has never once made it out of the limo since.

beats.line: At two a.m., the party moved to our roof. Kelly gave us until three. She was very clear about three.
Eleven fourteen on the dot. I have a time-stamped photo. Pay up.
You robbed a bride, Lily. You don't win by moving the clock.
Technically, he smiled at bumper cars in the limo. That's a crack. I'm claiming a crack.
Ted. One question. Did Schmosby break you tonight?
No. I chose him.
Then Schmosby never broke Ted. My slot was never. Lawyered.
Wait. I believe in you, buddy, was a betting strategy?
No, baby. It was totally sincere.
It was also a betting strategy.
Doesn't matter. Kelly confiscated the pot. For the cake.
That's fair. It was a very good cake.
From the back.
Nana Dot invited me to polka night at the Parma Elks Lodge. I said yes.
Ted, I'm so scared. I think I'm going to have a wonderful time.
Kelly told you about the suspensions, huh?
Nine, Punchy.
Ten. One she don't know about. Craig Dunleavy. Prom night. Called you Professor Dorkface.
Worth it.
Why didn't you ever tell me?
'Cause you'd thank me all fancy. Like Theodore.
I got a picture of your building on my fridge. I tell everybody in Parma my best friend made New York taller.
You know what's weird? You didn't correct a single person tonight.
Punchy said expresso four times. You just nodded.
It was so hard, Lily.
Theodore corrects waiters. Schmosby rode bumper cars for six hours with his best friend.
I like Schmosby better.
Me too, buddy. Bring it in.
Ow. Same arm. You even hug like a punch.
It's three.
Yes, ma'am.
Punchy and Kelly have renewed their vows three times since. I was best man every time. I've never made it out of the limo.
